quote: Recent studies use either few-shot manually constructed samples or zero-shot generalized refactoring instructions to create prompts that guide large language models (LLMs) in generating new samples from original sentences, increasing both the quantity and quality of the data.
In this paper, we propose a pipeline-based data augmentation method using LLM to enhance data diversity in sentence representation learning.

we propose a pipeline-based data augmentation method using LLMs and introduce the Gaussian-decayed gradient-assisted Contrastive Sentence Embedding (GCSE) model to improve the performance of unsupervised sentence embedding methods.
datasets: NLI dataset from Gao et al.
outputs: Generated positive and negative sentence samples for data augmentation in sentence representation learning

The paper generates synthetic positive and negative sentence samples using LLMs for data augmentation in sentence representation learning, such as rewriting sentences, creating syntactic antisense versions, and revising entities and quantities.

We evaluate model performance with Spearman's correlation on semantic textual similarity (STS) tasks, not on generated text quality.
